behavior_constraints: Add a `schedule` subcommand dispatched from main alongside existing subcommands without altering their behavior.

Validate the spec through the existing validation path; invalid spec exits 2 with stderr-only `error: <code>: <message>
` and empty stdout.
`--spec` missing exits 2 with non-empty stderr and empty stdout.

`--workers` missing exits 2 with stderr-only `error: --workers required
` and empty stdout.

`--workers` must be a decimal integer >= 1 with no leading +, no leading zeros (e.g. 01), no whitespace, no non-numeric; otherwise exit 2 with stderr-only `error: bad --workers
` and empty stdout.

`--format` must be in {text, json}; otherwise exit 2 with stderr-only `error: bad --format
` and empty stdout.
`schedule` does NOT support `--only`; passing `--only` or any unknown flag/positional exits 2 with non-empty stderr and empty stdout.
Compute schedule level-by-level in Kahn level order, byte-wise within each level, with unit-duration jobs (start=earliest, end=start+1).

earliest is the smallest timestep t such that every dependency has end <= t (0 if no deps); if all workers have busy_until > earliest, pick the worker with smallest busy_until (ties: smallest index) and set earliest = busy_until[w].
Worker selection iterates 0..N-1 picking first w with busy_until[w] <= earliest; record (name, worker, start, end).
entities.summary: This round adds a read-only `schedule` subcommand that validates a spec and emits a deterministic level-major byte-wise worker-lane assignment with unit-duration jobs in compact text or JSON form.

instruction_head:
# jobforge schedule

Add a new subcommand `schedule` that assigns every job to a worker lane
so the DAG can be executed in parallel, and emits the schedule as a
byte-exact text plan.

All existing behavior is unchanged.

## New subcommand: `jobforge schedule --spec <path> --workers <N> [--format text|json]`

Validates the spec (same error contract as `plan`/`list`/`hash`/
`diff`). `N` must be a positive integer `>= 1`. On success, computes
